- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 73.41 → 74.22 or 72.74 → 74.38), then corrects sharply.
- Underestimates in late forecast periods (last 5–10 days of 30d), suggesting mean reversion or lagged adjustment.
- Forecast mean is consistently higher than true mean by ~1–3%, indicating persistent upward bias.
- Model reacts too quickly to recent history, missing longer-term trend shifts (e.g., 70s → 73s → 75s → 77s).
- When history includes a strong upward trend, model overreacts and peaks too early.
- When history includes a strong downward trend, model underreacts and fails to anticipate drop.
- Forecast often lags true outcome by 1–3 days in the middle of the 30d window.
- Model exhibits “overfitting to recent highs” — forecasts peak too early after a spike.
- True outcomes often show “reversion to mean” after a spike, while model holds high forecast longer.
- Model underestimates when true outcome is below 70, especially after a spike above 75.
- Model overestimates when true outcome is above 75, especially after a spike below 70.
- Forecast tends to be smoother than true outcome, missing volatility spikes.
- Model fails to capture “reversal” patterns — e.g., 75 → 70 → 75, model predicts 75 → 75 → 75.
- Model often misjudges “turning point” — e.g., 73 → 70, model predicts 73 → 75 → 75.
- Model underestimates when true outcome is below 70 after a spike above 75.
- Model overestimates when true outcome is above 75 after a spike below 70.
- Model fails to adjust for “seasonal” or “calendar” effects — e.g., 70s in June, 75s in September.
- Model overestimates when history includes a strong upward trend, then underestimates when history includes a strong downward trend.
